summary: @bottino/baileys hardcodes WhatsApp pairing code, enabling session hijack
details: This fork of the @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp library replaces the normally-random device-link pairing code with a constant author-known value ('BYPAKI64') whenever the caller does not supply a custom pairKey. In lib/Socket, requestPairingCode falls back to assigning authState.creds.pairingCode = 'BYPAKI64', and that value is fed into derivePairingCodeKey during the pair-device key exchange with WhatsApp servers. The pairing code is a shared secret in the companion-device handshake; forcing it to a value known to the package publisher lets anyone who knows the installer's phone number pair an attacker-controlled companion device onto the installer's WhatsApp account, yielding message read/send access and session takeover. The package is published under a lookalike scope (@bottino/baileys) positioning it as a drop-in replacement for the widely-used baileys library, and internally identifies itself as 'Baileys by Sam aka Vare' — the delivery vector for the weakened handshake.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
